prompt: Order the sections of a weekly client status report in Word, top to bottom.

task.prompt: Drag the items into the right order, first at the top.

items.label: Summary: overall status and key message

task.explanation: Lead with the headline so a busy reader gets it at once; detail goes last.

prompt: This is the status slide for Acme's steering meeting. Mark the flaws.

task.prompt: Mark every segment that is a problem. Leave the sound ones unmarked.

segments.issue: Green contradicts a three-week go-live slip.

segments.text: Go-live moved from 1 Nov to 22 Nov (payment gateway delay).
Body text in 10 pt, 14 bullets, five colours.
segments.issue: Unreadable on screen; cut to the key points.

segments.text: Decision needed: approve an extra QA week by 10 Oct.
Risks: see the attached 40-row RAID log.
segments.issue: Top risks belong on the slide, not in an attachment.

segments.text: Next steps, each with an owner and date.

prompt: Order the steps for sending an SOW draft to a client for review.

task.prompt: Drag the items into the right order, first at the top.

items.label: Save as a new version number
Export the agreed version to PDF for signature
Go through their changes one by one: accept or reject
Make your edits, with comments explaining them
Send to the client for review

task.explanation: Track from the start, version it, review changes individually, sign a PDF.

prompt: Acme returned the SOW with tracked changes. Flag the changes you should not simply accept, then answer.

task.prompt: Flag changes that need discussion before accepting.
task.title: Word — Review › Tracked changes (Acme SOW v3)

rows.issue: A date change affects the plan; agree it first.

cells: Fixed a typo in the section 2 heading

rows.issue: Added scope: needs estimate and agreement.

cells: Deleted the Out of scope list
rows.issue: Removes your protection against scope creep.

questions.question: How should Priya know why you rejected c4?
options: A comment on the change, summarised in your reply email
Reject it silently
A phone call with no written record
questions.explanation: Leave a written reason where the change is, and summarise it.

prompt: A PM's notes on preparing an SOW in Word. Mark the practices that will cause problems.

task.prompt: Mark every segment that is a problem. Leave the sound ones unmarked.

segments.text: Section titles use Heading 1/2 styles, so the table of contents updates.

segments.issue: Use clear version numbers or version history, not file-name guesses.

segments.text: Scope lists in-scope and out-of-scope items.
Client's tracked changes accepted with Accept All, unread.
segments.issue: Every change must be reviewed; one may alter scope or price.

segments.text: Comments resolved with a reply explaining the change.
Page numbers typed by hand in the footer.
segments.issue: Use a page number field so they stay right.

segments.text: Sent to the client as a PDF for signature.

prompt: Acme returned your SOW with 23 tracked changes. Most are wording, but one changes "3 rounds of revisions" to "unlimited revisions".

steps.question: How do you handle the changes?
options: Review each: accept wording fixes, comment on the revisions change
Accept All to save time
Reject All and resend the original
Edit their text with tracking off
steps.explanation: Wording can be accepted; a commercial change needs a response.

steps.question: For the revisions change you:
options: Reject it with a comment proposing a middle option; tell your account lead
Accept it to keep the client happy
Delete the clause silently
Ignore it
steps.explanation: Unlimited revisions is open-ended cost; negotiate it in the open.

prompt: You're reviewing the steering deck before it goes to the client. Flag the slides to fix, then answer.

cells: Summary: status Amber, one decision needed
Burndown chart with no axis labels
rows.issue: A chart without labels can't be read.

cells: Top 3 risks with owners and mitigations

rows.issue: Summarise; move detail to an appendix.

questions.question: You'll email the deck after the meeting. Which format?
options: PDF, so layout and fonts hold
PPTX with your internal speaker notes
Screenshots pasted in the email
questions.explanation: A PDF looks the same everywhere and can't carry editable internal notes by mistake.

prompt: Acme sends back SOW v4 with no tracked changes: "just small edits". Signature is due tomorrow.

steps.question: How do you find what changed?
options: Word's Compare: your v3 against their v4
Trust them and sign
Skim both side by side
Ask them to list their edits from memory
steps.explanation: Compare shows every difference as tracked changes, whatever the client says.

steps.question: Compare shows payment terms changed from 30 to 60 days. You:
options: Raise it with the client and your finance or account lead before agreeing
Accept it as a small edit
Change it back silently
Ignore it; payment is finance's job
steps.explanation: A commercial change is never a small edit; agree it openly.

prompt: You want an automatic table of contents in Word. What must you do first?

options: Apply Heading styles to section titles
Make the titles bold
Number the pages by hand
Add a section break after each title
mcq.explanation: The table of contents is built from Heading styles; bold text is not picked up.

options: Records each insertion and deletion so others can accept or reject it
Locks the document
Saves a copy every hour
Logs who opened the file
mcq.explanation: It marks every edit with its author so changes can be reviewed one by one.

prompt: You need the client's logo and footer on all 30 slides. Best way?

options: Edit the Slide Master
Paste them onto each slide
Add a background picture per slide
Group all the slides
mcq.explanation: The Slide Master applies to every slide using its layouts, and new slides get it too.

prompt: Before sending a Word file that went through internal review to a client, you should:

options: Run Inspect Document to remove comments and tracked changes
Turn off spell check
Remove all styles
Convert tables to images
mcq.explanation: Inspect Document finds leftover comments, tracked changes and hidden content you don't want the client to see.
